problem:
The velocity $v$ at time $t$ of a particle $P$ moving in the $xy$-plane is given by

$$
v(t)=⟨\frac{2}{t+1},\,2t-5⟩,\,t\in (0,\infty ).
$$

Given that the particle is at the position $r=⟨0,6⟩$ when $t=0,$ find the times when the particle intersects the $x$-axis. Do not round the answers.

In **ascending order**, the particle intersects the $x$-axis when $t=$
{{field-1}}
and $t=$
{{field-2}}.
worked_solution:
The particle intersects the $x$-axis when its position is $r=⟨x,0⟩,$ where $x$ is arbitrary. So first, we need to compute the position function of the particle.

To compute the position vector, we need to integrate the velocity vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =\int v(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =\int ⟨\frac{2}{t+1},\,2t-5⟩\text{d}t \\  & =⟨\int \frac{2}{t+1}\,\text{d}t,\,\int (2t-5)\,\text{d}t⟩ \\  & =⟨2\operatorname{ln}⁡(t+1)+{C}_{1},\,{t}^{2}-5t+{C}_{2}⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can solve for the constants of integration using the fact that $r(0)=⟨0,6⟩.$ Substituting $t=0,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}r(0) & =⟨2\operatorname{ln}⁡(1)+{C}_{1},\,{0}^{2}-5(0)+{C}_{2}⟩ \\ ⟨0,6⟩ & =⟨{C}_{1},\,{C}_{2}⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we must have ${C}_{1}=0$ and ${C}_{2}=6.$ Therefore, the position of $P$ at time $t$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =⟨2\operatorname{ln}⁡(t+1),\,{t}^{2}-5t+6⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

To find the times when the particle intersects the $x$-axis, we solve for the times at which the $y$-coordinate of the position vector is zero:

$$
\begin{aligned}{t}^{2}-5t+6 & =0 \\ (t-2)(t-3) & =0 \\ t & =2,\,3.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, in ascending order, the particle intersects the $x$-axis when $t=2$ and $t=3.$
